Higher-order hypergraph from a network's clique structure

Source: R/hypergraph.R
build_hypergraph.Rd

build_hypergraph() turns a network into a hypergraph by promoting its cliques to hyperedges: every set of 3 to max_size nodes that are all tied to each other becomes a hyperedge, kept with probability p, and the pairwise edges can be kept as hyperedges of size 2. It takes a netobject, a bare cograph_network, a simplicial_complex or an adjacency or weight matrix, and returns a net_hypergraph, the input of the hypergraph verbs such as hypergraph_measures(), hypergraph_centrality() and clique_expansion().

A hyperedge built this way records that every pair of its nodes is tied in the thresholded network; a pairwise network cannot show whether those nodes also act together as a group. When group memberships are observed directly, bipartite_groups() builds the hypergraph from them instead. Each clique also contributes its smaller cliques: with max_size = 4, a 4-clique gives one hyperedge of size 4 and four of size 3.

Usage

build_hypergraph(
  net,
  p = 1,
  method = c("clique", "vr", "rips"),
  include_pairwise = TRUE,
  max_size = 3L,
  threshold = 0,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_hypergraph'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_hypergraph'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

net

The network: a netobject, bare cograph_network, simplicial_complex (its edges are read as ties of weight 1 and the cliques are found again up to max_size), or a numeric or logical adjacency or weight matrix (nodes are named V1, V2, ... when it has no row names). A tie counts in either direction, so a directed network is symmetrised, and self-loops are ignored.

p

The probability that each clique of 3 or more nodes becomes a hyperedge, a number in [0, 1]; each clique is kept or dropped independently. Default 1 (every clique is kept). Pairwise edges are not sampled.

method

How hyperedges are found. "clique" (default) promotes the cliques of the thresholded network. "vr" and "rips" (a metric Vietoris-Rips construction) are not implemented and raise an error instead of falling back to "clique".

include_pairwise

Whether the pairwise edges of the thresholded network become hyperedges of size 2. FALSE gives a hypergraph of hyperedges of size 3 or more only. Default TRUE.

max_size

The largest hyperedge size, at least 2. Default 3 (triangles); 4 adds the 4-cliques, and so on. With 2, only the pairwise edges remain (none, with include_pairwise = FALSE).

threshold

The cut-off that turns weights into ties: an edge is kept when its absolute weight is non-zero and at least threshold, so negative weights count by their size. A negative value raises an error. Default 0 (every non-zero weight is a tie).

seed

An integer that makes the sampling reproducible when 0 < p < 1. The session's own random stream is left as it was. Default NULL.

x

For the print() method: a net_hypergraph.

...

Not used.

object

For the summary() method: a net_hypergraph.

Value

A net_hypergraph object. print() shows the numbers of nodes and hyperedges, the size distribution and the settings, and returns its input invisibly. summary() prints the counts with the mean and largest hyperedge size, and returns a data frame with one row per node: node and degree, the number of hyperedges that contain it. The object holds:

hyperedges

A list of integer vectors, one per hyperedge, each the sorted indices of the nodes it spans; pairwise edges, when kept, come first.

incidence

An integer matrix of nodes by hyperedges, 1 where a node belongs to a hyperedge and 0 elsewhere. Its row names are the node names and its column names h1, h2, ...

nodes

The node names.

n_nodes, n_hyperedges

The numbers of nodes and hyperedges.

size_distribution

A named integer vector with the number of hyperedges of each size, named size_2, size_3, ...

params

The settings used: method, p, include_pairwise, max_size, threshold and seed.

Details

The construction follows Burgio, Matamalas, Gomez and Arenas (2020) on cooperation in networks and hypergraphs. The cliques are found with build_simplicial(), and each clique of 3 or more nodes then goes through an independent Bernoulli(p) trial that decides whether it becomes a hyperedge. The pairwise edges are not sampled: with include_pairwise = TRUE all of them are kept, so the hypergraph holds the pairwise structure and the sampled higher-order interactions together.

At the limits:

  • p = 0 with include_pairwise = TRUE gives the thresholded pairwise network as a hypergraph of size-2 edges.

  • p = 1 with include_pairwise = FALSE gives only the hyperedges of size 3 or more, every clique of the network's clique complex up to max_size.

References

Burgio, G., Matamalas, J. T., Gomez, S., & Arenas, A. (2020). Evolution of cooperation in the presence of higher-order interactions: from networks to hypergraphs. Entropy 22(7), 744. doi:10.3390/e22070744

See also

build_simplicial() (the clique enumeration), bipartite_groups(), build_network().

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 8
adj <- matrix(stats::rbinom(n * n, 1, 0.5), n, n)
diag(adj) <- 0
adj <- (adj + t(adj)) > 0
rownames(adj) <- colnames(adj) <- LETTERS[seq_len(n)]
hg <- build_hypergraph(adj, p = 1, max_size = 3L)
print(hg)
#> Hypergraph: 8 nodes, 51 hyperedges
#> Size distribution:
#>   size_2   : 23
#>   size_3   : 28
#> Method: clique, p = 1.00, include_pairwise = TRUE, max_size = 3
summary(hg)
#> Hypergraph summary
#>   Nodes:         8
#>   Hyperedges:    51
#>   Mean size:     2.55
#>   Max size:      3
#>   node degree
#> 1    A     17
#> 2    B     17
#> 3    C     23
#> 4    D     17
#> 5    E     17
#> 6    F     13
#> 7    G     13
#> 8    H     13
